5e84c1b128062479: PASIR MAS: The Kelantan Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) has handed over four of the 12 General Operations Force (GOF) control posts constructed under Phase One of the Sungai Golok Integrated River Basin Development Project (PLSB), which began in 2018.
Kelantan DID director Datuk Dr Siti Fairus Zakaria said the two most recent facilities handed over were the Kaloi and Wakaf Zin control posts in Pasir Mas, which were completed on July 12.
She said two other facilities, the Pok Teh Kana and Pak Atah control posts, were handed over to the GOF in September last year.
"The control posts were built to provide GOF personnel with more comfortable, safe and systematic facilities to carry out border security and monitoring duties in Kaloi and Wakaf Zin.

"It is hoped that these facilities will strengthen monitoring and control along Sungai Golok while supporting the government's efforts to safeguard national security and sovereignty," she said at the handover ceremony for the Kaloi Control Post today.
Siti Fairus said the handover of the remaining eight control posts was expected to complete the network of GOF operational facilities in the border areas.
She said the 12 control posts were built at a total cost of about RM9 million, or around RM800,000 each.
She said the development of the facilities also supported an integrated river basin management approach encompassing river management, flood control and border security.
"Hopefully, the control posts will contribute to stronger border security while safeguarding the well-being of the local community," she said.

d40df51533956cd2: OCTOBER 26 — The political fortunes of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, popularly known as Lula, have implications far beyond Brazil.

His continued leadership, through a victorious re-election, would offer Brazil another opportunity to deepen its engagement with Malaysia, Asean and the wider Global South. Brazil is after all a sectoral partner of Asean.
Brazil and Malaysia are geographically distant but strategically closer than conventional diplomacy might suggest. The forest in the Amazon and Borneo respectively needs fine stewardship.
Both are important emerging economies, members of the Global South, and countries that have consistently sought greater autonomy in a world dominated by competing major powers.
More importantly, both countries understand that the international order is undergoing profound structural changes.

The United States remains powerful, China continues to expand its economic and technological influence, and the traditional institutions of global governance are struggling to accommodate the aspirations of developing nations.
Against this background, another Lula presidency could reinforce the convergence between Brasília and Kuala Lumpur.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim with Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva gesture after a press conference following their bilateral meeting at Seri Perdana Complex in Putrajaya October 25, 2025. — Bernama pic
First, Lula has long represented a political tradition that places economic development, social inclusion and strategic autonomy at the centre of Brazilian foreign policy.
His political philosophy is not identical to that of Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Yet both leaders recognise that economic growth cannot be sustained without social legitimacy, institutional stability and a reasonable distribution of national prosperity.
Both also understand that developing countries cannot afford to become permanent extensions of the geopolitical preferences of Washington or Beijing.
Brazil’s strategic autonomy is rooted in Latin America’s historical experience. Malaysia’s is anchored in ASEAN’s commitment to regional centrality, diplomatic flexibility and open regionalism.
These different historical trajectories nevertheless produce an important convergence: neither country wishes to be trapped in a rigid international bloc.
Second, Brazil’s engagement with Malaysia should move beyond the familiar confines of commodity trade.
Brazil is a major agricultural producer, with considerable strengths in soybeans, beef, poultry, biofuels and agricultural technology.
Malaysia possesses substantial expertise in palm oil, Islamic finance, halal certification, electronics and semiconductor-related manufacturing.
There is considerable scope for cooperation between these complementary economic structures.
Malaysia’s halal industry, for example, could provide Brazil with opportunities to strengthen its access to Muslim consumer markets across Southeast Asia, West Asia and Africa.
Conversely, Brazil’s agricultural productivity and technological capabilities could contribute to Malaysia’s food security and agricultural modernisation.
Such cooperation would be especially valuable when global supply chains remain vulnerable to geopolitical disruptions, maritime insecurity and fluctuations in energy prices.
Third, Malaysia and Brazil should recognise the strategic significance of BRICS.
Brazil is a founding member of BRICS, while Malaysia has pursued closer engagement with the grouping through its partner-country status.
This creates an important diplomatic opening.
Malaysia need not regard BRICS as an alternative to Asean. Nor should Brazil view Southeast Asia merely as another destination for its exports.

Instead, both countries can explore how BRICS and Asean might complement one another in advancing financial cooperation, infrastructure development, technological exchanges and reforms of international institutions.
Lula has consistently argued for a more representative international economic order.
Anwar has similarly advocated a more equitable global architecture that gives developing countries a stronger voice.
Their convergence should be translated into practical cooperation rather than confined to diplomatic declarations.
Fourth, the relationship between Brazil and Malaysia can become an important bridge between Latin America and Southeast Asia.
These two regions have traditionally maintained stronger economic relationships with the United States, China and Europe than with one another.
Such patterns are increasingly outdated.
Brazil is the largest economy in Latin America, while Asean collectively represents one of the world’s most dynamic economic regions.
Malaysia, positioned at the intersection of the Indian and Pacific Oceans, can serve as a useful gateway for Brazilian companies seeking greater engagement with Southeast Asia.
Brazil, in turn, can help Malaysian enterprises understand the opportunities and complexities of Latin American markets.
The objective should not merely be to increase bilateral trade figures.
It should be to create sustained institutional relationships between universities, research centres, chambers of commerce and strategic policy communities.
Fifth, technological cooperation deserves greater attention.
Brazil has developed important capabilities in aerospace engineering, agricultural research, renewable energy and industrial technology.
Malaysia is seeking to strengthen its position in artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, advanced manufacturing and semiconductor supply chains.
There is no reason why these respective strengths cannot become the foundation of a more ambitious bilateral technological partnership.
Indeed, both countries must confront the dangers of technological dependency.

The rapid concentration of artificial intelligence capabilities in a small number of American and Chinese corporations raises fundamental questions about data sovereignty, economic autonomy and the future of employment.

Brazil and Malaysia have a shared interest in preventing the emergence of a new form of digital colonialism in which developing countries become consumers of technologies they neither control nor meaningfully regulate.
Sixth, environmental cooperation should become another strategic pillar.
Brazil possesses the Amazon rainforest, while Malaysia is home to some of the world’s most important tropical ecosystems.
Both countries face international pressure over deforestation, biodiversity protection and the environmental consequences of agricultural expansion.
Yet both must also defend the legitimate developmental aspirations of their populations.

Rather than accepting environmental standards formulated without sufficient consideration of developing-country realities, Brazil and Malaysia should cooperate in promoting sustainable development based on scientific evidence, equitable financing and technological assistance.
This is particularly important when environmental regulations risk becoming instruments of disguised protectionism.
Seventh, both countries have an interest in preserving diplomatic space amid escalating global conflicts.

5e547fc55747d4df: PETALING JAYA, Oct 26 — The Kuala Terengganu High Court has upheld the dismissal of a RM400,000 negligence and defamation suit filed by a former student against her teachers and the government over a body search and the seizure of her mobile phone during an SPM trial examination six years ago.

Judicial Commissioner Yusrin Faidz Yusoff dismissed Nur Nabilah Ahmad Zambala’s appeal and upheld a Sessions Court decision that threw out her suit against two teachers, a school principal and the government, Berita Harian (BH) reported.

The court ruled that while the school was entitled to confiscate Nabilah’s mobile phone, it had no authority under Education Ministry guidelines or school examination regulations to inspect its contents.
“Although the phone was indeed evidence, lawful possession of evidence does not automatically confer the authority to access its digital contents,” Yusrin was quoted as saying.

The case stemmed from an incident on October 25, 2020, when teachers conducted a spot check following complaints that Nabilah had cheated during a Sains Rumah Tangga SPM trial examination at SMK Sura in Dungun, Terengganu.
Checks on the phone uncovered notes, examination questions and answer schemes for several subjects.
However, Yusrin held that the procedural breaches did not amount to negligence, ruling that the teacher had acted reasonably in investigating allegations of cheating.
He also said identifying the source of the leaked examination questions and answer schemes was a more serious issue than the student’s possession of a mobile phone during the examination.

2ddafd6b0691bde4: GEORGE TOWN: A 73-year-old doctor killed in a landslide yesterday died from blunt-force trauma and breathing difficulties, according to post-mortem findings.
Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the victim suffered the injuries after being crushed by earth.
"The findings indicate that the victim suffered blunt-force trauma and breathing difficulties after being crushed by earth," he said when met at the scene.

Dr Wong Kar Lin was found partially buried after the landslide caused a wall of his house to collapse on him. https://www.nst.com.my/amp/news/nation/2026/10/1562964/man-killed-landslide-paya-terubong-house
His 68-year-old wife and 86-year-old mother-in-law escaped unhurt.
Rozak said police had cordoned off the affected area and were guarding six houses evacuated on safety grounds.
The displaced residents are staying at hotels, while police personnel will remain at the scene to prevent unauthorised entry into the vacated homes.
He said the duration of the security deployment had yet to be determined, pending a technical meeting with the local authority.
"The area remains closed due to the risk of further landslides, particularly with rain expected in the coming days.

"Based on the advice of technical experts, rainfall could trigger another landslide. We advise residents and members of the public to follow police instructions and stay away from restricted areas," he said.
Rozak said police received a call from the victim's family shortly after the landslide and responded with the Fire and Rescue Department in an attempt to rescue him.
He said the case remained under investigation as a sudden death report (SDR), despite the post-mortem findings.
7aba4571ce78809d: JOHOR BARU: Johor plans to extend Visit Johor Year 2026 into next year following an increase in tourist arrivals this year, Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said.
He said Johor recorded 4.7 million tourist arrivals from January to June and was confident of reaching its target of 12 million tourists staying in the state by the end of the year.

"Our target is 12 million tourists staying in Johor, generating an economic impact of RM42 billion. Based on figures for January to June, we have recorded 4.7 million tourist arrivals and are on track to achieve the target," he said at the Visit Johor Year 2026 public dialogue here today.
Onn Hafiz said next year would be a game changer for Johor, particularly with the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link.
The RTS Link will connect Johor Bahru and Singapore and is scheduled to begin operations in February next year.
Onn Hafiz said from 2022 to this year, the state had spent RM187 million on tourism products and expected to spend at least another RM50 million next year.

4e302a5693afc9ad: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The High Court’s decision to grant leave to 12 Ampang Jaya residents to initiate judicial review proceedings challenging the Ampang Jaya Municipal Council Local Plan 2035 (RT MPAJ 2035) marked a significant step forward for local community rights.
In a statement, residents’ action group TOLAK RT2035 claimed that the local plan, gazetted on Feb 6, 2025, contained fundamental flaws and unpublicised land-use conversions.
They further claimed that the local plan did not incorporate the objections raised during the 2022 public objection hearing.
It said the court allowed the leave application, filed in May last year, after finding that the challenge raised arguable questions of law and fact warranting a full judicial hearing.
“We believe that the local plan currently permits high-intensity developments in environmentally sensitive areas on hilltops and hillslopes, and established disaster-risk zones.
“Unsustainable developments threaten terrain stability, escalate risks of severe landslides and flash flooding, and destroy the remaining natural environment,” the group said.

TOLAK RT2035 identified Bukit Antarabangsa, Taman Hillview, Ukay Perdana, Taman Melawati, Kemensah, and Taman Ukay Heights among high-risk zones facing pressure from proposed intensive and mega developments.
According to the statement, leaving the plan unchallenged would erode the public’s statutory right to object to future projects under the Town and Country Planning Act 1976.
The hearing for the substantive judicial review application has been set for Nov 25. — Bernama
62631d304d83f261: MELAKA: Datuk Azman Abidin will prioritise identifying and resolving outstanding issues in Paya Rumput after being named as the candidate for the state seat last Saturday.

Azman, who is the Prime Minister's political secretary, said he recognised that every constituency had its own challenges, including problems that might not have been fully resolved by the previous assemblyman during the five-year term.
He said identifying outstanding issues was important to finding solutions and improving areas that still required attention.
"Everywhere, there are issues raised by the people, and we acknowledge that the previous assemblyman has played his role.
"Some issues may not have been resolved because not everything can be settled within five years.

"God willing, I will try to find solutions to any outstanding issues and improve the situation," he said after the closing ceremony of Minggu Melaka Ceria at Padang Dewan Bunga Tanjung, Tanjung Minyak, last night.
Asked about perceptions that he was an outsider in Paya Rumput, Azman said he was from Melaka, although his family was based in Kuala Sungai Baru, Masjid Tanah.
He said not being from the constituency should not prevent him from serving its residents.
"I went to school in Melaka, and my family is from the state. I am not from Paya Rumput constituency, but from the neighbouring Masjid Tanah area.
"What matters is that we can serve the people of Paya Rumput," he said.
Azman said his decision to contest in Melaka was also driven by a desire to contribute to the state, which was linked to his family's roots.
Although he had never contested in an election before, he viewed the opportunity as a chance to serve the state.
fe4b967641223bca: KANGAR: A government retiree pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to three charges of committing physical sexual assault and criminal force against two girls about two months ago.
Annuar Abdullah, 72, entered the plea after the charges were read out to him before Judge Sharifah Norazlita Syed Salim Idid.

The first two charges alleged that Annuar committed physical sexual assault for sexual purposes against an 11-year-and-five-month-old girl at a house at No. 7, Lorong 4 Jalan Utama here, at 6.30 pm on Aug 11.
The third charge alleges that he used criminal force against a 10-year-and-11-month-old girl by pulling both her legs with the intention of outraging her modesty, at the same place, time and date.
The first two charges were brought under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
The third charge, under Section 354 of the Penal Code, carries a maximum prison sentence of 10 years, a fine, whipping, or any two of the punishments, upon conviction.
The court granted Annuar bail of RM10,000 with one surety and ordered him to report to a nearby police station on the first day of every month.
He was also prohibited from approaching or disturbing the victims and prosecution witnesses until the disposal of the case.
The court fixed Nov 24 for mention for submission of relevant documents.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohd Alif Farhan Hassan prosecuted, while Annuar was represented by lawyers Zuhair Ahmad Zakuan and Mohamad Alif Farhan Mohamad Supian.

3b3a84c8cec43170: KUALA LUMPUR: Ministers must fulfil their promises to provide written answers to parliamentary questions.

Dewan Rakyat speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said ministers should inform their respective ministry secretaries-general whenever they commit to submitting written replies to ensure the answers are delivered within the stipulated period.

"Do not simply make a promise in this House without informing your officers, as they may not be aware of it. Therefore, I am giving five days for the replies to be submitted," he said during the Dewan Rakyat sitting.
Johari said he had records of ministries that had failed to provide written answers despite having made such commitments.

"Please take this matter seriously. If any secretaries-general are listening to this, whenever a minister says they will provide a written answer, please take immediate action to ensure that the commitment is fulfilled," he said.
He said the answers were often ready and only needed to be sent to the MPs who had raised the questions.

cc14810597ba5222: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Awards are nice, but Datin Sofia Jane has her sights set on something she considers far more valuable: another 20 years of doing what she loves.

The veteran actress is nominated for Best Supporting Actress at the 35th Malaysian Film Festival (FFM 35) for playing Sarimah, a woman whose unsettling presence and troubled past lie at the heart of horror film Malam Terlarang.
“I think being able to continue working is what defines me,” she told Malay Mail in a recent interview.
For Sofia, recognition is welcome, but the real reward is getting to take on characters that challenge her understanding of people and push her into unfamiliar territory.
“I think I'm defined by what I do, what I work on, who I work with, and whether I'll still be able to work for another 20 years, God willing, if I live that long,” she said.
That appetite for the unfamiliar drew her to Sarimah, the mother of Mawar (played by Shasha Abedul) in the film directed by the late Nurhanisham Muhammad, better known as Labu.
Sarimah is a woman who seems almost invisible in her own home, moving through a space that should offer comfort and familiarity while those around her barely acknowledge her existence.
For Sofia, that disconnect raised intriguing questions about a character who is physically present but appears emotionally and socially erased.
She was also drawn to Sarimah's history as a dancer, a part of her past that audiences never actually see on screen.
Sofia wanted to explore what it might mean for someone who once could walk, dance and jump to lose those abilities, and how that loss might reshape her sense of self.
The role offered a chance to delve into the character's inner life rather than simply play the horror film's supernatural elements.
For Sofia, that willingness to venture into the unknown is part of what keeps acting worthwhile, whether the end result brings an award or simply a new perspective.
“It's lovely to be recognised, but you still have to continue working and looking for something you've never done before, something you don't understand but want to understand,” she said.
Malam Terlarang, produced by Astro Shaw, received 12 nominations at FFM 35, tying with Shamyl Othman's Khadam as the ceremony's joint-leading nominee.
FFM 35 will take place at Panggung Sari, Istana Budaya, Kuala Lumpur, on November 21.
5f7f8a1bc3aebce7: KUALA LUMPUR: : Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah missed out on the French Open women's doubles title after impatience in attack crept into their game, national coach Rosman Razak said.
Japan's world No. 3 Yuki Fukushima-Mayu Matsumoto recovered to beat the fourth-ranked Malaysians 10-21, 21-17, 21-16 in 63 minutes at Arena Grand Paris on Sunday to retain their crown.
The defeat ended Pearly-Thinaah's bid for back-to-back Super 750 titles following their Denmark Open victory the previous week.
Rosman said their early tactic of varying shot placement and patiently constructing attacks worked against the Japanese pair, but they struggled to maintain discipline as the match wore on.
"In the second and third games, the desire to finish rallies quickly and impatience in attack began to affect the stability of our defensive system," Rosman said.
"At the same time, several simple errors gave the Japanese pair opportunities to build sizeable leads."
Rosman said the physical strain of back-to-back tournaments also took a toll on Pearly-Thinaah, adding that recovery is now the priority as they manage existing injuries.
"This week was always expected to be more difficult because they had expended so much physically during last week's tournament," he said.
"Nevertheless, I am proud of their mentality and fighting spirit. Despite facing various injury problems, they continued to show a high level of commitment on court.
"I am grateful that we have managed to keep their injury situation under control so far. However, the main focus now is ensuring their recovery goes well."
Rosman did not specify the injuries, but said the defeat should not overshadow the pair's performances over the fortnight.
"This was not the result we had hoped for, but I remain proud of Pearly-Thinaah's achievements, effort and spirit over these two weeks," he added.
"We know there is still room for improvement. We are not yet at our best and will continue to work hard, learn from every match and prepare better for upcoming tournaments."

cf846732712bbd91: KUALA LUMPUR: Jorge Martin, who lost the championship lead to Marc Marquez at Phillip Island, is in a race against time to be fit for the Petronas Grand Prix of Malaysia which starts on Friday.
Aprilia Racing team manager Paolo Bonora said that Martin's injury is not as bad as initially feared and the team is "working" to get him fit in time for Sepang.
Martin crashed while duelling with Marquez (Ducati Lenovo) during the sprint race at Phillip Island on Saturday.
Martin fractured his right wrist during the crash.
"He was in attack mode and there were many overtakes, he showed that he has very good race pace (during sprint race)," Bonora told MotoGP.
"But to be honest the crash was huge. We are checking over the next few days how the evolution of his situation is.
"At the moment, it seems that surgery is not necessary, which is positive news. We just have to wait and see how the situation evolves.
"We will absolutely work for it (to race at Sepang) and he (Martin) is the first to work towards this goal.
"But we have to wait for the medical updates. We are only engineers, we have to follow the medical analysis, but we are quite positive about that."
Aprilia disclosed that Martin had undergone a CT scan to assess his condition which confirmed that he had suffered a non-displaced fracture of the distal radius.
The team also confirmed that Martin will not be returning to Spain.
Martin, who had a two-point lead over Marquez heading into the Australian round, now trails the latter by 10 points.
Marquez was, however, unable to extend his lead over the weekend as the main race at Phillip Island on Sunday was cancelled due to poor visibility.
Martin's teammate Marco Bezzecchi is third overall, 50 points adrift of Marquez.
Ducati team principal Davide Tardozzi is also hoping to see Martin race at Sepang.
"I wish Jorge that he will be able to race in Malaysia," Tardozzi told MotoGP.
"I think he will make a huge effort (to do so), he will try very hard to race to save some points, but we will see.
"I think that Jorge is a fantastic rider, he is a hero and he can do something special for himself."
Marquez will no doubt look to press his advantage as Sepang's long straights have suited Ducati machinery very well, and it is no surprise they have dominated the Malaysian GP since 2022.

eff7e498e88e459c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad was unable to attend the SG4 Business and Economic Forum 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre today due to health reasons.

His son, Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir, said the 101-year-old statesman had prepared his keynote speech and intended to deliver it himself, but had been feeling unwell in recent weeks, Berita Harian (BH) reported.

“He worked hard on this speech and very much wanted to deliver it himself. Unfortunately, his health has not been at its best lately, and I am honoured that he asked me to present this keynote address on his behalf,” Mokhzani said when delivering the speech at the forum.
Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir was also present.

In the speech read by his son, Dr Mahathir apologised for his absence and said he had yet to make a full recovery, although he was grateful to still be able to share his views with participants through the prepared text.
No further details about his condition were disclosed.
Dr Mahathir, who serves as an adviser to SG4, had been scheduled to deliver a special address at the forum.
b498de13dd8bccf9: KUANTAN: The Pahang government is looking to expand direct shipping services to Sabah and Sarawak beyond wheeled vehicles to include containers, in a move to reduce logistics costs for businesses.

State Investment, Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Nizar Najib said the first roll-on/roll-off (RoRo) vessel carrying 17 vehicles departed Kuantan Port on Oct 19 and arrived at Kuching Port in less than 48 hours.
The service marked the revival of direct shipping links between Kuantan and East Malaysia, decades after the now-defunct Feri Muhibbah ended operations about 30 years ago.

"For the first time since the ferry service ended, we have a shipping operator, Konsortium Perkapalan Timur, transporting vehicles directly from Kuantan to ports in East Malaysia. I was told the company would deliver 300 vehicles this week," he told reporters after opening Pahang Export Day 2026 here today.
Nizar said automotive companies in Pahang currently relied on lorries to transport vehicles to Port Klang before shipping them to Sabah and Sarawak, a journey that takes between four and six days.
"The RoRo service takes only one day and 19 hours," he said.
Also present was Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) chief executive officer Datuk Indera Abu Bakar Yusof.
Feri Muhibbah was the country's largest cruise ferry and operated between 1986 and 1989, linking Kuantan Port with Sabah and Sarawak. It could carry up to 1,000 passengers, along with vehicles.
Nizar said he hoped the shipping operator would eventually expand its services to include container shipments, as businesses in Kuantan and Pekan still relied on Port Klang to transport their goods.

"Businesses should leverage Kuantan Port to ship goods to Sabah and Sarawak, potentially reducing logistics costs and delivery times by making better use of the facilities available in Pahang," he said.
He said the state government aimed to develop Kuantan Port into a world-class facility, with the long-term ambition of placing it among the world's top 10 ports.
"To achieve this, export volumes through Kuantan Port must increase, and exporters across the east coast should be encouraged to use the facility," he said.
In his speech earlier, Nizar said the Pahang government planned to strengthen trade ties with Sarawak by expanding two-way trade cooperation.

He said both states would explore opportunities for small and medium enterprises to trade their products, including Pahang's ikan patin and sambal hitam, while Sarawak could supply products such as salted terubuk fish and kek lapis to Pahang.
"This would encourage more local businesses to explore markets beyond their home states. We might explore energy exports," he said.
f6387045304ae94e: KUCHING: The 13th Sarawak election will be less about determining who will form the state government and more about how far the opposition can erode the dominance of Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS), which enters the election with an overwhelming political advantage.
At the previous state election in 2021, GPS won 76 of the 82 state assembly seats, while Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) won four seats and DAP secured two.

However, the state assembly's composition changed after the election when See Chee How left PSB to become an independent assemblyman, before three other former PSB assemblymen — Datuk Seri Wong Soon Koh, Dr Johnical Rayong Ngipa and Baru Bian — joined Parti Demokratik Progresif (PDP), a GPS component party.

These developments have given GPS control of 79 seats. Another former PSB assemblyman, See Chee How, chose to remain an independent who supports the government, bringing the government bloc and representatives aligned with it to 80 of the 82 seats. DAP holds the remaining two seats, Padungan and Pending.

With the state assembly dissolved with effect from today, the key question in the coming state election is no longer whether GPS can form the government, but whether it can retain most of the 76 seats it won in the previous polls.
Of Sarawak's 82 state constituencies, between 45 and 50 are considered GPS safe seats, while another 20 to 25 are classified as grey seats that favour the ruling coalition.

The safe seats, where GPS has a very strong chance of retaining control, include most of Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu's (PBB) traditional strongholds, as well as several constituencies held by PDP and Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS), where the coalition secured large majorities in 2021.
These include Tanjong Datu, Pantai Damai, Demak Laut, Tupong, Samariang, Satok, Asajaya, Muara Tuang, Stakan, Sadong Jaya, Simunjan, Gedong, Sebuyau, Saribas, Bukit Saban, Kalaka and Kabong.

Other constituencies where GPS has a strong chance of retaining control are Kuala Rajang, Semop, Daro, Jemoreng, Nangka, Dalat, Tellian, Balingian, Katibas, Bukit Goram, Jepak, Kemena, Bekenu, Lambir, Telang Usan, Mulu, Bukit Kota, Batu Danau and Bukit Sari.

Constituencies such as Daro, Dalat, Tupong and Bukit Sari also recorded large winning majorities in 2021, making it particularly challenging for the opposition to unseat GPS incumbents without an extraordinary shift in voter sentiment.
Another 20 to 25 constituencies are seen as favouring GPS but will require considerable effort to retain, as they fall within the grey category.
These seats cannot be considered entirely safe, particularly if there are changes in candidates, stronger opposition performances or shifts in voter sentiment.

They include Opar, Tasik Biru, Serembu, Mambong, Tarat, Tebedu, Kedup and Bukit Semuja, where the results of the 12th state election showed that some constituencies had relatively narrow winning margins.

Several constituencies in the central and southern regions, including Lingga, Beting Maro, Simanggang, Batang Ai, Layar, Krian, Pakan, Meluan, Ngemah and Machan, are also projected to fall into the grey category.

At the same time, GPS is not taking its advantage for granted. PBB information chief Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said the party was confident of retaining at least a two-thirds majority and had the potential to win three-quarters of the seats.
However, he acknowledged that certain constituencies required particular attention, given several current factors, including the possibility of changes in candidates.
The participation of opposition parties, including Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Pas, is expected to pose a challenge that should not be underestimated.

The presence of several local parties, including Parti Bansa Dayak Sarawak (PBDS), Parti Aspirasi Rakyat Sarawak (ASPIRASI), Parti Wawasan Rakyat and Parti Bumi Kenyalang, could also add to the contest.

b5a381a41a19cd56: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — In a world of endless scrolling and on-demand entertainment, Datin Sofia Jane wants audiences to do something increasingly rare — put their phones away, sit in the dark and let a story get to them.
The actress returns to the stage next month in Thrown, a one-woman play about childhood trauma, buried memories and the emotional baggage people carry into adulthood.
Written by Jodi Gray and directed by Gavin Yap, the production sees Sofia play a child psychologist whose patients’ experiences begin to blur with memories she has kept buried in her own past.
For Sofia, the play’s appeal lies in how it explores the ways painful experiences can shape not only our lives but also our relationships with others.

“When I read it, I thought it was very interesting because we are living in a world where mental health challenges affect not just adults but people of all ages, from children to the elderly,” she told Malay Mail in a recent interview.
One actress, one stage, no hiding place

Taking on an entire production alone is no small feat, particularly in a story that demands a performer move between a psychologist’s professional world and the personal memories she has spent years avoiding.
Sofia admitted that carrying an hour-long performance on her own was both daunting and exciting.
“Everything is a challenge,” she said.
Although her work in film and television has kept her busy, Sofia said she never lost her appetite for theatre, with the right role and timing simply not always lining up.
“Being on stage is something I always look forward to because it has a different energy,” she said.
“It feels like starting all over again.”
Can theatre compete with the scroll?
For Sofia, the appeal of live performance is precisely what makes it different from watching a film or series at home: audiences have to show up, pay attention and experience the story as it unfolds.
She believes theatre still has a place in Malaysia’s entertainment landscape, with younger creatives exploring how sound, lighting and music can push the form in new directions.
But keeping the stage alive also means confronting practical barriers, including whether people can afford tickets and whether they are willing to give a performance their undivided attention.
Theatre, she added, is not confined to contemporary plays or urban audiences, encompassing traditional forms such as Bangsawan, Mak Yong and Indian classical dance.
“We often say theatre is for everyone, but affordability can be an issue,” she said.
For Sofia, the responsibility of sustaining the art form does not fall solely on performers and producers; audiences must also be willing to make room for it.
“It comes down to whether people can afford to attend, whether they want to go and whether they are willing to put their phones down for a while, sit in the dark, listen and watch,” she said.
“The experience might trigger something in them, whether good or bad, or give them something to reflect on.
“That is part of why we do what we do.”
When the curtain falls, the conversation continues
There is another aspect of live theatre that Sofia believes is difficult to replicate on a screen: the conversations that happen after a performance.
In an intimate venue, audience members may linger to exchange thoughts about what they have watched, how it made them feel and what they took away from the experience.

“People often linger after a theatre performance, sometimes waiting for the actors to come out, but also because they want to talk to others about what they have seen and how it made them feel,” she said.
That shared experience is part of what keeps theatre meaningful for Sofia, even as entertainment habits change.
Thrown will run at the Jeffrey Cheah Performing Arts Centre in Sunway City, Petaling Jaya, Selangor, over two weekends, from November 20 to 22 and November 27 to 29.
Tickets are available through CloudJoi.

62057dbdde85b043: BRUSSELS: The European Union will from Nov 1 slap a €2 (US$2.25) handling fee on packages from outside the 27-nation bloc in a bid to curb the influx from China.
The new levy -- coming just weeks before the Black Friday, Cyber Monday, and Christmas season shopping rushes -- will be on top of the EU's three-euro fee on small parcels.

The fee will apply to each type of item in a package sent directly to consumers from outside the EU regardless of the parcel's value. For example, if there are 10 T-shirts in a package, the handling fee will be €2.
But if a package contains two hats and 10 T-shirts, the fee will be €4.
The handling fee comes on top of the €3 duty imposed in July on small packages worth less than €150.
But European consumers will not pay the handling fee, insists the EU.
Online marketplaces including US platforms such as Amazon and Chinese retailers such as AliExpress and Temu, as well as sellers and other intermediaries must pay the new fee.
Platforms and sellers can, however, raise their prices, thereby passing off the higher costs to the consumer.
Why is the EU introducing the fee?
Nearly six billion small packages entered the EU last year, according to official data.
Some 93% of the cheap packages that arrived in Europe came from China, usually via popular Asian platforms such as AliExpress and Temu.
Brussels says this is putting increasing strain on customs authorities to manage this influx, thereby raising their costs too. The handling fee will compensate their efforts.
Since the EU imposed the €3 duty on small parcels in July, imports have fallen by around 64% -- although officials warn it is too early to draw firm conclusions.
Europe has also expressed concern about "unsafe" non-EU products such as toys that violate the rules arriving in the bloc via Chinese e-commerce platforms.
The €2 handling fee is a permanent levy but the three-euro duty on low-value packages is a temporary measure in place until July 1, 2028.
From that date onwards, standard, product-specific customs tariffs will apply.
The EU will have to assess the handling fee's amount every two years to ensure it remains proportional to the cost of customs operations in the bloc.

ea0a609eccce2eec: PUTRAJAYA: A 39-year-old Perak-born man with five Malaysian children has failed in his bid to be recognised as a Malaysian citizen after the Court of Appeal ruled that he had not met the constitutional requirements for citizenship.
A three-member panel chaired by Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli dismissed Velmurugan's appeal, with Datuk Faizah Jamaludin and Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz also sitting.

The court found that although Velmurugan had lived in Malaysia all his life, he had failed to prove that his biological mother was a Malaysian citizen or that he was not born a citizen of any country.
Velmurugan was born on Feb 24, 1987, at Ladang Escot in Ulu Bernam, Tanjung Malim, Perak.
However, his birth was only registered on May 24, 2011, when he was already 24.

Following an investigation, the National Registration Department (NRD) issued him a birth certificate recording his citizenship status as "unknown", while his mother Balamah was listed as a non-citizen.
Balamah, who was said to have been born here on Dec 31, 1952, also had her birth registered late in 2019.
The NRD recorded her citizenship status as "not determined" after finding inconsistencies in witnesses' accounts concerning her birthplace and family background.
In September 2023, an application was submitted to the NRD to amend Velmurugan's birth certificate to reflect his status as a Malaysian citizen and include his mother's birth certificate number.
The department approved the inclusion of his mother's details but rejected the application to change his citizenship status.
Velmurugan challenged the decision through judicial review, but his application was dismissed by the High Court on May 19 last year.
In affirming the decision, the appellate court said there was insufficient evidence to establish that Balamah was a Malaysian citizen.
The judges noted that witnesses had given conflicting accounts of whether she was born in Kuala Lumpur or Tanjung Malim, while there were also discrepancies concerning the number of her siblings.
The court said the fact that Balamah's siblings were Malaysians did not establish her citizenship, as they had obtained their nationality through different registration procedures.

"The entitlement to Malaysian citizenship and all matters related thereto must be determined based on the constitutional requirements under Part III of the Federal Constitution," the court said in its grounds of judgment published by the Judiciary Department recently.
It also noted that there was no evidence establishing whether Velmurugan's biological parents were legally married at the time of his birth.
The judges also dismissed Velmurugan's reliance on Article 19 of the Federal Constitution, which provides for citizenship through naturalisation.
Velmurugan had argued that he had lived in Malaysia since birth, was of good character and had never been involved in criminal activities.
However, the court said naturalisation required a separate application to the federal government, which had the discretion to grant citizenship upon fulfilment of the constitutional requirements.
It also found no evidence that the NRD had acted unlawfully, irrationally or unreasonably in rejecting his application.

"We have carefully examined the affidavits filed in the court below, and we are of the view that the impugned decision was not tainted by illegality, irrationality, procedural impropriety or even disproportionality," said the court.
Velmurugan was represented by lawyers Annou Xavier and Callista Chin, while federal counsel Safiyyah Omar appeared for the respondents.

7c639435b84a1ea3: KUALA LUMPUR: Nurul Izzah Anwar has warned that companies controlling the algorithms shaping people's lives lack an ethical foundation.
"It's bad enough that it's governed by algorithms and not the word of God. The problem is, the companies that own these algorithms have no ethical basis whatsoever," she said.
Nurul Izzah, executive chairman of the Suluh Centre and PKR deputy president, was speaking at the opening of the third Southeast Asia Dialogue Cities Conference here.

Also present were KAICIID International Dialogue Centre senior project manager Mitra Modaressi, Allied Coordinating Council of Islamic NGOs Malaysia (ACCIN) chief executive officer Ir Mohd Jamaludin Shamsudin and Universiti Antarabangsa MAIWP (UniMAIWP) vice-chancellor Professor Dr Mohd Afandi Salleh.
Nurul Izzah described the impact of algorithms on the mind as one of the biggest "fitnah" (trials or tribulations) facing the current generation, adding that it affected everyone, not just Muslims.
The three-day conference, organised by KAICIID and ACCIN, carries the theme "Shared Futures: Dialogue for Resilient and Inclusive Cities".
More than 65 participants from Bangkok, Davao, Kuala Lumpur, Singapore and Yogyakarta are attending, including religious, youth and women leaders, as well as civil society representatives.
Modaressi said people in the region spent about 11 hours a day on their digital devices, leaving them increasingly isolated.
She said urbanisation in Southeast Asia was growing at 2.2 per cent a year, twice the rate of population growth, as millions moved to cities in search of better lives.
"True dialogue is the simple, radical act of reaching across the aisle. It is a bridge built between the wisdom of our elders and the fire of our youth," she said.

59a8437751d21b3a: KUALA LUMPUR: A cabin crew member pleaded not guilty in the magistrates’ court today to two charges of driving under the influence of alcohol, causing the death of one person and injuries to another in an incident on Oct 24.

The charge, under Section 44(1A)(b) of the same Act, carries a prison term of between seven and 10 years and a fine of between RM30,000 and RM50,000, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Fadhly Zamry proposed bail of RM25,000 for each charge, as well as the suspension of Iman’s driving licence and the impounding of his passport until the case concludes.

cfef8af57139db77: KUALA LUMPUR: Data centre engineering services provider MyDCD Bhd expects to raise RM187.6 million from its initial public offering (IPO) ahead of its listing on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market on Nov 17.
The company today launched its IPO prospectus, offering shares at 56 sen apiece, with the listing expected to give it a market capitalisation of about RM1 billion.

The IPO comprises a public issue of 335 million new shares to raise RM187.6 million for the company and an offer for sale of 145 million existing shares through private placement, expected to raise RM81.2 million for the selling shareholders.
Of the proceeds from the public issue, RM134 million will be used for working capital, primarily to support project execution and fund performance bonds.

Another RM39.9 million will go towards expanding operations through additional recruitment, office rental and staff training, while RM5 million will be allocated to enhance information technology systems.
The balance will cover listing expenses.

MyDCD, which specialises in integrating mechanical, electrical, plumbing and fire protection (MEPF) systems for critical infrastructure, particularly data centres, recorded revenue of RM666.03 million and net profit of RM66.8 million for the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY26).
Revenue and net profit grew at a compound annual growth rate of 52.8 per cent and 58.48 per cent respectively between FY23 and FY26.
As at Sept 30, the company had an outstanding order book of RM1.32 billion, equivalent to about 1.98 times its FY26 revenue.
Of the total, RM1.27 billion came from data centre MEPF integration projects, while RM53.08 million was from maintenance services.
The order book is expected to be progressively recognised as revenue up to FY32.
The company also provides maintenance services and parts for completed data centres, with 76 active maintenance contracts as at Sept 30.
These contracts typically last between one and five years.

MyDCD chief executive officer Chris Ow Yong said the company's experience in data centre projects across Tier I to Tier IV classifications had helped it establish long-standing relationships with key customers, some spanning about 15 years.
Its work covers the MEPF integration process, from engineering support, supply and installation to testing and commissioning.
"As project requirements become more demanding, having the right technical capabilities, experienced personnel and working capital is essential," he said in a statement.
Ow Yong said the IPO proceeds will support project execution, including performance bonds, while strengthening the company's workforce and systems to support growth.

According to an independent market research report in the IPO prospectus, Malaysia's MEPF construction market grew at a compound annual growth rate of 15 per cent between 2023 and 2025, reaching RM10.4 billion in 2025.
The market expanded by a further 18.1 per cent in the first half of 2026 from the same period a year earlier.
Malaysia recorded RM385.7 billion in data centre-related investments between 2021 and the first half of 2026.
Ow Yong said growing artificial intelligence adoption was increasing data centres' requirements for computing power, cooling and energy management, making MEPF systems increasingly important.
The company will focus on strengthening its execution capabilities to meet evolving customer requirements and pursue opportunities as the industry develops.
TA Securities Holdings Bhd head of corporate finance Ku Mun Fong said the listing would strengthen MyDCD's corporate profile and provide access to capital for its next phase of development.
Applications for MyDCD's IPO opened today and will close on Nov 2 at 5pm.
TA Securities is the principal adviser, sponsor, underwriter and placement agent for the IPO.
MyDCD's shares have been classified as Shariah-compliant by the Securities Commission's Shariah Advisory Council.

be5ba6ae22d3c29f: PETALING JAYA: The Court of Appeal has ordered GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH) to pay RM5,000 in costs to the Attorney-General’s Chambers for a 27-day delay in filing its appeal record in a challenge to a Selangor fatwa declaring it deviant from Islamic teachings.

A three-member Court of Appeal panel chaired by Justice Zaini Mazlan made the ruling after hearing submissions from GISBH and the AGC, which represented the Selangor fatwa committee and the Selangor Islamic Religious Council as respondents.

Lawyer Zulfikri Ulul Azmi, representing GISBH, sought an extension of time to file the appeal record, saying his team was unaware that a draft index had not been submitted. He said the error had since been rectified.
Federal counsel Sallehuddin Ali, representing the respondents, opposed the application.
"We maintain our position as stated in our submissions and leave the matter of costs to the court," he was quoted as saying by Berita Harian.

After hearing submissions from both parties, Zaini, sitting with Justices Ong Chee Kwan and Radzi Harun, allowed the application for an extension of time and ordered GISBH to pay RM5,000 in costs to the AGC immediately.

The appeal relates to the Shah Alam High Court’s decision in January to dismiss GISBH’s application for leave to initiate a judicial review challenging a fatwa issued by the state fatwa committee and gazetted on Oct 16, 2024.

In her grounds of judgment, High Court judge S Narkunavathy ruled that the challenge to the fatwa could not proceed through a judicial review in the civil courts, as the matter fell under the jurisdiction of the shariah court.
She referred, among others, to Article 121(1A) of the Federal Constitution, which limits the jurisdiction of civil courts over matters within the jurisdiction of the shariah court.
The High Court also examined the nature of the fatwa, which, according to the grounds of judgment, was directed at GISBH’s Muslim leaders, followers, employees and members.

In its memorandum of appeal, GISBH challenged the decision, arguing that its application did not seek to have the civil courts determine questions of Islamic law, but rather to examine the validity of the fatwa and the process through which it was issued.
It also raised questions about the implementation of a fatwa against a corporate entity such as GISBH.

On Oct 18, 2024, the Selangor fatwa committee issued a fatwa declaring GISBH an organisation that promotes deviant teachings, after finding that its wider network practised the teachings of the Darul Arqam group, which was banned in 1993.

d5e17ab5c2ece69d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Scammers are using fake discounts, countdown timers and bogus preorder pages to trick buyers hoping to get their hands on Apple’s newly launched iPhone Duo, cybersecurity firm Kaspersky warned today.
The fraudulent websites mimic Apple’s visual style and promise discounts of up to 25 per cent, while some claim to offer early access to the foldable phone that officially went on sale on October 23.
“Scammers move fast when a flagship device hits the market, because hype creates urgency and urgency lowers caution,” Kaspersky senior web content analyst Olga Altukhova said.

She said the schemes were designed to appear credible before moving potential victims into private conversations, where they might be less likely to verify the seller’s identity or the legitimacy of the offer.

Kaspersky said its researchers had detected scam attempts targeting buyers in different parts of the world, with tactics ranging from collecting personal details through fake checkout pages to pushing potential victims into private messaging conversations.

According to Kaspersky, one English-language website had advertised a 25 per cent discount and displayed a countdown timer claiming the offer would expire in 30 minutes, pressuring visitors to act quickly.

The site asked customers to submit their contact details and delivery address but did not request payment information immediately, instead claiming that a manager would contact them later to confirm delivery and payment arrangements.

In another case targeting Portuguese-speaking users, a fraudulent website asked visitors for the phone number linked to their WhatsApp account and their email address to check the device’s availability.

Other fake sites offered multilingual interfaces, allowed users to select their preferred currency and promoted supposed preorders, with one claiming buyers would be redirected to Apple’s official website even though this did not happen.

Such tactics expose personal contact details and could leave victims vulnerable to follow-up scams and social engineering, in which fraudsters manipulate people into revealing sensitive information or taking actions that benefit the scammers.
Kaspersky advised consumers to buy new devices only from official or reputable retailers and check website addresses carefully before sharing personal information.

It also recommended using virtual cards or dedicated payment services for online purchases, enabling two-factor authentication on accounts and financial apps, and monitoring bank statements for unauthorised transactions.

Consumers should also be wary of unusually attractive discounts, unofficial preorder offers and requests to confirm product availability by sharing personal details, particularly when dealing with unfamiliar sellers.

e03637ee13b2fea3: SEPANG, Oct 26 — The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) has developed hologram technology to be deployed at the satellite building of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1, to assist travellers in obtaining information regarding arrival procedures in the country.

AKPS deputy director-general (management) Ismail Mokhtar said this initiative is part of the agency’s efforts to leverage technology to make it easier for travellers to access necessary information upon their arrival in Malaysia.

He noted that the development of this hologram was inspired by an initiative from the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN), which installed a hologram of the Minister of Home Affairs, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, in the lobby of the Setia Perkasa Complex.

“Just as the Ministry of Home Affairs placed a hologram of the Minister in the lobby of the Setia Perkasa Complex, AKPS shares the same vision and mission. We have created a hologram to be stationed at the KLIA satellite building, which will provide arriving travellers with information on the requirements they need to fulfil upon entry into the country,” he said.
He made these remarks while speaking at the AKPS 2nd Anniversary Celebration held here today, which was officiated by the Ministry of Home Affairs secretary-general, Datuk Dr. Awang Alik Jeman.
In a separate development, Ismail said AKPS aims to have 1,259 containers carrying electrical and electronic waste (e-waste) exported out of the country by the end of this year.
He explained that this target follows the government’s successful export of e-waste containers earlier this year, a feat achieved for the first time through a task force led by the agency.

“The issue of e-waste importation demonstrates that the threats at the nation’s entry points are becoming increasingly complex. Enforcement goes beyond merely detaining containers, it encompasses document verification, technical inspections, identifying the parties responsible, and monitoring follow-up actions,” he said.
During the event, AKPS also launched its 2026–2030 Strategic Plan, which serves not only as a reference document but also as an operational guide for its officers.
Additionally, AKPS unveiled a new logo featuring a red eagle symbolising the agency’s sharpness and state of readiness with a sundang (a traditional sword), representing courage and discipline.

Meanwhile, Awang Alik noted that the Minister of Home Affairs, who was initially scheduled to attend the celebration, could not be present due to an urgent, unavoidable assignment that arose at the last minute.
He mentioned that Saifuddin Nasution extended his apologies to all AKPS personnel for being unable to join in the celebration of the agency’s second anniversary.
“The Honourable Minister also expressed his apologies to everyone present today, as he was tasked at the last minute with an extremely important and unavoidable duty,” he said.

He added that the Minister of Home Affairs conveyed his regards, along with his congratulations and appreciation to all AKPS personnel, for their commitment and dedication in upholding the trust placed in them to safeguard the nation’s security and border sovereignty.
Earlier, the absence of both Saifuddin Nasution and AKPS director-general, Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, drew the attention of the press.
On October 21, Mohd Shuhaily was charged in the Magistrate’s Court with two counts of causing injury to two police officers.

On October 24, Saifuddin Nasution reportedly said the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN) has entrusted matters concerning the position of the director-general of AKPS to the secretary-general of the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Chief Secretary to the Government, Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar. — Bernama

"Ningbo is already a special place. Last year I started to play really well from this tournament. Hopefully it's going to give me motivation and good energy to continue this season and start the next one."
After losing nine of her first 13 finals, Rybakina has now won 11 of her last 15.
"I remember I was getting upset always losing in finals," she said after winning her fourth title of the year and 15th overall.
"Now it's going my way, but I can't expect it all the time ... now it's experience clicking in important moments."
Rybakina plays in the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo this week before heading to Indian Wells for the November 8-15 WTA Finals, where she went unbeaten last year to pocket over $5 million in prize money.

7cd3db64bb718f4f: GUA MUSANG, Oct 26 — Orang Asli living in remote areas have been urged to move to safe locations immediately if faced with the threat of floods, sudden torrents or landslides during the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), without waiting for conditions to become critical.

Kelantan and Terengganu Orang Asli Development Department (JAKOA) director Mohd Faedzyal Mohamed said all Tok Batin (Orang Asli village heads), penghulu (sub-district chiefs) and Orang Asli Village Development and Security Committees had been instructed to step up preparedness for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon, which is expected to begin tomorrow and last until March next year.

He said the directive followed a statement issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department on Oct 23, which forecast three to five episodes of continuous heavy rain between November 2026 and January 2027.
Mohd Faedzyal said village leaders needed to identify high-risk areas, monitor weather changes and river levels, and identify residents who might require immediate assistance during emergencies.

“These conditions could lead to flooding, particularly in areas near rivers and low-lying terrain. Residents must remain vigilant and prioritise the safety of themselves and their families,” he told Bernama today.
Mohd Faedzyal also advised residents to avoid using roads or bridges that were damaged, collapsed or eroded, and not to cross fast-flowing rivers or rivers where water levels were rising rapidly.

Sufficient supplies of food, clean drinking water, medicines and other essentials should be prepared, while important documents should be kept in a safe place in case evacuation became necessary, he advised.

Meanwhile, Galas assemblyman Datuk Mohd Syahbuddin Hashim said more than 1,000 Orang Asli heads of households in Pos Bihai, Pos Belatim, Pos Balar and Pos Hau were at risk of being cut off during the monsoon season because the dirt roads in the areas were vulnerable to heavy rain.
He said routes at Bukit Pasir, Bukit Kelabu, Bukit Sabun and Bukit Piyel needed regular maintenance to reduce risks to road users.
Mohd Syahbuddin also advised residents to avoid travelling during heavy rain and to contact JAKOA if they required emergency assistance. — Bernama
f39b6de5b4134ea4: KUALA LUMPUR: The Haj Preparation Plan – Seruan Istito'ah aims to strengthen financial preparedness among prospective pilgrims and ensure they meet the financial requirements to perform the pilgrimage.

Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the initiative reflected the original vision behind the establishment of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), conceived by the late Royal Professor Ungku Aziz, which emphasised financial discipline and early planning.
"This is precisely the spirit we are upholding: instilling financial discipline and encouraging prospective haj pilgrims to plan ahead so they can gradually build up their financial capacity.

"This is in line with the aspirations behind TH's establishment, as envisioned by Ungku Aziz, and the Islamic requirement that haj is obligatory only for those who are financially capable," he said during the winding-up session on the 2027 Supply Bill in the Dewan Rakyat.

Earlier, several opposition MPs called on the government to reconsider the RM15,000 minimum savings requirement under Seruan Istito'ah. They also raised concerns that existing depositors on the haj waiting list could lose their places if they failed to meet the threshold.
Among those who raised the issue were Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man (PN-Kubang Kerian) and Datuk Idris Ahmad (PN-Bagan Serai).
Under the initiative, depositors with a minimum savings balance of RM15,000 will automatically qualify to join the haj waiting list without having to register manually.
Existing depositors who have already registered for haj have until Dec 31, 2028, to meet the minimum savings requirement.
Addressing claims that TH operates like a bank, Zulkifli said the institution was bound by the mandate set out in the Tabung Haji Act, which defines its responsibilities and obligations.
"TH will continue to act in accordance with and comply with its mandate and will not undertake activities beyond that mandate," he said.
He added that the RM15,000 minimum savings balance remained eligible for annual profit distributions, allowing depositors to benefit from TH's profit-sharing arrangements while preparing for haj.
Earlier, Idris said TH should not operate like a bank, adding that it was not a commercial banking institution.
"When you deposit RM15,000, how much profit can you generate from it? This reflects the mindset of bankers, who focus on profitability.
"But we need to return to the original spirit behind TH's establishment. What was its founding principle? It was to help people in rural communities," he said.
Zulkifli said TH's experience had shown that many prospective pilgrims were inadequately prepared, with more than 50 per cent of those offered places requesting to defer their pilgrimage.
"This situation affects the efficiency of haj allocation and queue management, requiring TH to issue replacement offers repeatedly within a short period," he said.

He added that the initiative was also consistent with recommendations by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI), which proposed increasing the muassasah registration amount and raising the minimum qualifying deposit to reflect current costs.
"Do the Honourable Members of the House disagree with the RCI's recommendations, when this is the spirit we are seeking to uphold?" he said.
d61253e82c5c8c78: PETALING JAYA: The Kuantan High Court has reduced a housekeeping supervisor’s sentence for assaulting and robbing his former girlfriend to six years’ imprisonment and two strokes of the cane.
Judicial commissioner Kumar Thangaraju ruled that the original sentence imposed on Abdul Mu’izz Zin, 35, of 10 years’ imprisonment and three strokes of the cane was excessive.
The court upheld his conviction under Section 394 of the Penal Code for assaulting the 32-year-old woman while robbing her of her car at her home in Rompin on Aug 5, 2023.
According to the facts of the case, Mu’izz went to the woman’s house after their relationship ended and demanded money, allegedly for wedding preparations.
She told him to leave and returned to her room, leaving the sliding door open in case she needed to escape because she felt unsafe.
Later, she heard the car engine starting and tried to stop Mu’izz from driving away. During the struggle, he punched her, pushed her into the car and drove off.

He returned to the house after realising that he had left his mobile phone behind. He pushed the woman out of the car and told her to look for his phone, prompting her to run to her brother-in-law for help.
Police arrested Mu’izz in Kuala Lumpur and recovered the car in Johor Bahru.
Kumar said the conviction was safe as there was "no material discrepancy going to the heart of the charge".
"The accused’s own evidence in cross-examination deserves considerable weight. That evidence confirmed almost every element of the offence," he said.

On sentencing, Kumar said six years’ imprisonment properly reflected the gravity of the offence, noting that the woman’s injuries were relatively minor. A doctor found bruising on both cheeks and her right thigh, but no skull fracture. She was given paracetamol and anti-inflammatory medication.
No weapon was used, and the car was recovered intact within four days, he said.
d24d58f6cd5c62bb: RIYADH, Oct 26 — The Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis struck several of its missile launchers and storage facilities, a spokesman said today, while the Iran-backed group claimed a new attack on Riyadh’s international airport.

The coalition’s operation came a day after explosions rattled Saudi Arabia’s capital and authorities sent text messages to residents warning them of a “hostile aerial threat” to the city, which has been heavily targeted by the Houthis in recent weeks.

The Saudi-led military coalition’s spokesman Turki al-Maliki posted on X on Monday that the operation had destroyed four ballistic missile launchers, as well as a missile depot and tunnels used by the Houthis, who control a large part of Yemen.
The operation “focused on cutting off Houthi militia supply lines between areas under their control,” he added.

The group have carried out waves of strikes on the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, including an attack this month that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.
“Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh,” al-Maliki also said today.
The airport re-opened and fights resumed on Sunday with the Houthis warning travellers to avoid the facility, calling it a “military target.”

Today, the Houthis said once again they had attacked the airport “with a ballistic missile, striking the target with precision”, according to a post by Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree on social media.
He said the Houthis had also struck oil pumping stations with drones.
On Sunday, the Houthis had said they launched an attack on the airport in Riyadh, after the kingdom announced flights were resuming.

The airport closure had been a major blow for Saudi Arabia, forcing the postponement of the kingdom’s flagship investment conference until 2027 and disrupting travel plans for thousands of passengers.
The Dakar Rally also joined a growing list of events that were cancelled, postponed or relocated in the fallout from the war.
Saree had warned that Riyadh airport was still “unsafe” and a “military target”.
“The Saudi regime shall bear the consequences of any operations at the airport,” the spokesman said.

Saudi Arabia and the government it backs in Yemen have come under sustained attack in recent weeks from the Houthis as a years-long truce broke down in the summer, shifting the focus of the wider US-Iran war that erupted in February.
‘Everything is shaking’
As operations resumed at Riyadh airport, Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis met Saudi de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and discussed a key air defence system.
Mitsotakis “responded favourably to the kingdom’s request to keep the Patriot system in Saudi Arabia, given the current challenging circumstances”, his office said.
Greece has deployed a battery to operate the US-made Patriot air defence system in Yanbu, a major oil export hub on the Red Sea coast.
Yesterday, the Saudi-led military coalition said air defences intercepted at least 10 ballistic missiles.

“The bombardment has been very heavy since this morning — may God keep us safe. Everything is shaking because of the explosions,” one resident in Saudi Arabia’s Khamis Mushait told AFP yesterday on condition of anonymity.
The kingdom’s civil defence agency later said two people were injured in the south by falling debris, also reporting damage to several buildings and vehicles.

Images released by the kingdom’s official press agency showed a building with part of its upper facade destroyed, exposing metal rods. Another image captured large windows shattered, with shards of glass strewn across the pavement and part of the road. — AFP
07278838f78e43a5: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Court of Appeal judge and prominent lawyer Datuk Mahadev Shankar has died at the age of 94.
Former Malaysian Bar president Christopher Leong confirmed his death, describing Mahadev as one of the leading legal minds of his generation, both at the Bar and on the Bench.
"His recognition by the Bar as a recipient of the Malaysian Bar's Lifetime Achievement Award in 2014, the Bar's highest award, says it best of the man, lawyer and jurist that he was," he said.
Born in 1932, Mahadev was admitted to the Malayan Bar in 1956 and went on to build a distinguished legal career.
He was appointed a High Court judge in 1983 and elevated to the Court of Appeal in 1994 before retiring from the judiciary in 1997.
He was also a founding member of the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam), serving as a commissioner from 2000.
Mahadev served on the Royal Commission of Inquiry established in 1999 to investigate injuries suffered by Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim while in police custody.
He was also a member of the 2007 Royal Commission of Inquiry into the VK Lingam video clip controversy involving alleged interference in judicial appointments.
In 2014, he received the Malaysian Bar Lifetime Achievement Award for his contributions to the legal profession.
In a memorial tribute, the Gandhi Memorial Trust Malaysia described Mahadev as a man who dedicated his life to justice with courage, eloquence and unwavering humanity.
The trust said he embodied the ideals of Mahatma Gandhi, particularly truth, service and human dignity, leaving behind a legacy of wisdom, integrity and grace for generations to come.

02a5ac3a466ecd55: BEIJING, Oct 26 — President Xi Jinping opened a key meeting of Communist Party elites in Beijing today, state media said, which observers will be closely watching for clues as to the country’s direction and future leadership.

Roughly 300 members of the ruling Communist Party’s Central Committee in attendance at the meeting, called the fifth plenum, will be looking to tighten discipline within their ranks, according to state media.
That includes measures to reduce corruption and make cadres more effective and loyal.

Xi opened the session on Monday, presenting a draft decision by the Central Committee that “sets out strategic plans for strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance”, state news agency Xinhua reported.
Few details from the closed-door gathering, held under tight security, will be made known until it concludes on Thursday, but the timing of the meeting is crucial.
The fifth plenum comes ahead of a major party congress next year, where 73-year-old Xi is almost certain to secure a historic fourth term and oversee a leadership reshuffle.
Previous plenums have represented key moments for Xi to cement his authority.
The Chinese leader has waged a 14-year campaign against corruption that has purged thousands of officials, including dozens of the Central Committee.
Yet he remains frustrated with cadres he deems are not implementing his orders.

State media published an article ahead of the plenum, based on a speech Xi gave in January in which he railed against “two-faced” officials who appear to comply with central directives but “inwardly resist”, pursue “individualism” and are “politically opportunistic”.
Analysts told AFP that Xi is trying to maximise efficiency and loyalty among cadres by imposing more supervision and rules.
But as a result of his expansive purges, this year’s plenum is expected to have the lowest turnout since former leader Mao Zedong’s death in 1976.
Eight of the Central Committee’s seats lie vacant, with another 15 members under investigation and at risk of being replaced.
Xi’s anti-corruption drive has also targeted the military, toppling five of the seven members of the Central Military Commission (CMC), the party’s top armed forces body.
Of 44 military members appointed to the Central Committee in 2022, only two have not been purged or disappeared, according to the Asia Society Policy Institute.
The plenum could see new members appointed to the CMC; the party could wait until next year’s congress to replenish it; or Xi might even restructure party control over its vast military.

The talks also come at an unsteady time for the world’s second-largest economy, which has struggled to address persistently sluggish domestic spending and a protracted crisis in the crucial property sector.
Turbulent political and economic ties with the United States are also weighing on China’s leaders.
Authorities are expected to release a summary of the outcomes after the meeting concludes on Thursday. — AFP
ff8064324ceb5ec1: KUALA LUMPUR: Nine consecutive final defeats since early last year have not dented Lai Pei Jing's determination to secure a title.
The mixed doubles shuttler resumes her title pursuit with Hoo Pang Ron at the Hylo Open in Saarbrucken, Germany, starting tomorrow.
Pei Jing has finished runner-up seven times with former partner Jimmy Wong and twice with Pang Ron across 2025 and 2026.
Her last title came at the 2022 Korea Open with Tan Kian Meng.

Last year's near-misses with Jimmy included the Macau Open, the Korea Masters, both Indonesia Masters tournaments, and three lower-tier events — the Vietnam International Challenge, the Phuket International Series, and the St Denis Reunion Open.
With Pang Ron, she has reached the China Masters and French Open finals this season, losing both to China's world No. 1 pair Feng Yan Zhe-Huang Dong Ping.
Despite Sunday's 21-10, 21-13 defeat in France, Pei Jing remained upbeat about their progress.
"Every time we meet them, we try a new strategy, but they are really too tough for us," said Pei Jing.
"But we won't give up until we beat them one day."
Pang Ron-Pei Jing enter the Super 500 Hylo Open having reached the Denmark Open semi-finals and French Open final in consecutive weeks.
Although recent results have been encouraging, Pang Ron said clearer tactical planning and sharper communication are needed to strengthen their partnership.
"We need to discuss more about the strategies," he said.
"Sometimes we still have some misunderstandings. Hopefully, we will get better."
Pang Ron-Pei Jing open their campaign in Germany against qualifiers.
